questions.enonce_markdown:
8. What were the causes of the First World War? How was Germany treated at the end of the war?

**(10/10marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The First World War (1914-1918) broke out when Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914 and the alliances of Europe drew in the great powers. Its causes are usually divided into long-term causes and the immediate cause.

**1. Causes of the war (10 marks).**

**Long-term causes.**
- **The alliance system.** Europe was divided into two armed camps: the **Triple Alliance** (Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy, from 1882) and the **Triple Entente** (France and Russia, allied by 1894, with Britain joined to France by the Entente Cordiale of 1904 and to Russia by the agreement of 1907). A quarrel between two states could involve all.
- **Militarism and the arms race.** The powers built big armies and fleets, and conscription and war plans (such as the German Schlieffen Plan) made war easier. The naval race between Britain and Germany after the launch of HMS Dreadnought (1906) increased distrust.
- **Imperial and economic rivalry.** Germany, a new power, wanted "a place in the sun"; rivalry for colonies and markets caused crises such as the **Moroccan crises of 1905 and 1911**.
- **Nationalism.** Slav nationalism in the Balkans (Serbia, supported by Russia) threatened the multinational empire of Austria-Hungary; French desire to recover Alsace-Lorraine, lost in 1871, kept France and Germany hostile. The **Bosnian crisis (1908)** and the **Balkan Wars (1912-1913)** raised tension.

**Immediate cause.**
- On **28 June 1914**, the Archduke **Franz Ferdinand**, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, was assassinated at **Sarajevo** by **Gavrilo Princip**, a Bosnian Serb nationalist.
- Germany gave Austria-Hungary a "blank cheque" of support in early July; Austria sent an ultimatum to Serbia (23 July) and declared war on 28 July; Russia mobilised to defend Serbia; Germany declared war on Russia (1 August) and on France (3 August); the German invasion of **neutral Belgium** brought Britain into the war on **4 August 1914**.

**2. How Germany was treated at the end of the war (10 marks).**
- Germany asked for an **armistice**, signed on **11 November 1918**, after the Kaiser had abdicated and revolution had broken out in Germany.
- The peace was settled at the **Paris Peace Conference (1919)** by the Allied leaders, **Woodrow Wilson** (USA), **Georges Clemenceau** (France) and **David Lloyd George** (Britain). Germany was not allowed to take part in the discussions and was obliged to sign the **Treaty of Versailles on 28 June 1919**; Germans called it a *diktat* (dictated peace).
- **War guilt:** by **Article 231**, Germany had to accept responsibility for causing the war.
- **Reparations:** Germany had to pay for the damage of the war; the sum was fixed in 1921 at 132 billion gold marks.
- **Loss of territory:** Alsace-Lorraine returned to France; Eupen-Malmedy went to Belgium; part of North Schleswig to Denmark; the Polish Corridor and most of Posen and West Prussia to Poland; Danzig became a free city under the League of Nations; the Saar was placed under the League for fifteen years. Germany lost about 13% of her land and all her colonies, which became **League of Nations mandates**.
- **Disarmament:** the army was limited to 100,000 men without conscription, tanks or an air force; the navy was cut down and had no submarines; the **Rhineland** was demilitarised and occupied by Allied troops for up to fifteen years.
- **Union with Austria** was forbidden.

**Conclusion.** The war was caused by the alliances, militarism, imperial rivalry and nationalism, with the Sarajevo assassination as the spark; the harsh treatment of Germany at Versailles left deep resentment that was later used by Hitler.
